newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FORECAST-Merger overshadows Boland results.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Merger overshadows Boland results.

text.p: Analysts have discounted Boland Bank's year-end results due next week ahead of its merger with fellow South African financial services group NBS and its delisting from the Johannesburg Stock Exchange.
"Its immaterial and we are looking at the combined group now," one analyst said, echoing responses from several others.
Some analysts had reservations about the merger, which comes into effect on May 1 creating the country's fifth biggest banking group.
They said they expected some "indigestion" in the year ahead as the new group assimilated the different parts of the two institutions.
There was also concern about the group's planned pioneering move into in-store banking, first with Pick 'n Pay Stores Ltd and then with retailer Shoprite Holdings.
"They might lose some market share to their competitors while they try and sort out their mission statement and where they are going," a banking analyst said.
"The novelty of in-store banking also still has to take off in the country."
It was seen difficult for the new group, to be called NBS Boland Ltd, to show strong earnings growth in the first year because of its large investment in financial group The Board of Executors Ltd.

"That has a high PE and will dilute the earnings to some extent. So it depends on the cost savings that they are going to achieve in the first year, which is usually difficult to achieve in a short space of time.
"It is more the second year earnings where you should start seeing those benefits come through. The first year will probably show 20 percent (growth)."
In a complex deal announced last month NBS Boland bought a 24.3 percent stake in BOE. BOE in turn purchased 22.2 percent of NBS's shares.
The link with BOE was expected to boost NBS Boland's share price, improving ratings, while BOE would be able to use the NBS client base to cross-sell products.

Only one analyst out of ten polled could provide a forecast for Boland results due next Wedneday. He expected earnings to rise to 272 cents per share on a diluted basis from 211 cents and the dividend to 92 cents from 77.7 cents before.
He said profits would be boosted by the new group structure and earnings flow after the purchase of a 45 percent stake in brokerage Senekal Mouton and Kitshoff Securities.
A further boon was an improved capital adequacy ratio which would up margins and the performance of the new Boland Bank-PKS holding company.
A feature of the results could be the benefits of Boland's purging of its loan book over the last 18 months, with the writing off of bad debts.
"But we are going to be talking about a different entity in another months' time," an analyst said.
